summary: Addendum No. 1 moves the bid due date three days earlier, to Monday, March 15, 2027 at 2:00 p.m., and now requires bid security of 5 percent of the bid price with every bid. It also says boilers from another manufacturer will be considered if a written request for approval is received by 5:00 p.m. on Monday, March 8, 2027, and it must be acknowledged on the Bid Form.

settles.text: The original did not say whether boilers from a manufacturer other than the one named in the specifications would be accepted. The addendum says they will be considered if a written request for approval of an equal, with product data, is received by the Purchasing Office by 5:00 p.m. on Monday, March 8, 2027.

notes.text: The due date moves earlier, not later: bids are now due three days sooner. The deadline for written questions stays at 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, March 10, 2027, which is now five calendar days before bids are due.
notes.section: 2. Change to the bid due date

notes.text: A bid submitted without bid security will be rejected. Only the first sentence of Section 5 is replaced, so the performance and payment bonds and the certificate of insurance required of the successful bidder still apply.

Asking to use a boiler from a different manufacturer is optional, but it has its own deadline: the written request, with product data, must be received by 5:00 p.m. on Monday, March 8, 2027, two days before the questions deadline. The addendum does not say when or how the District will answer.
A bid that does not acknowledge this addendum on the Bid Form may be rejected.
The addendum says the Board moved its March meeting forward by one week, but the bid date moves by three days, not seven. The two statements do not conflict; I read March 15 as the date that holds.
